title: Reach a Number
summary: Starting at position 0 on an infinite number line, you aim to reach a destination at position target.
statement: Starting at position 0 on an infinite number line, you aim to reach a destination at position target. You can make a series of moves, moving either left or right. On the i-th move, you take i steps in the chosen direction. Determine the least number of moves needed to reach the target.
constraints: On move k choose +k or -k; return the fewest moves needed to reach target from zero.
reference_solution:
def minimum_reach_steps(target):
    target=abs(target);distance=steps=0
    while distance<target or (distance-target)%2:steps+=1;distance+=steps
    return steps

hints: Changing one +k to -k reduces a triangular sum by the even amount 2k.
Find the first triangular sum at least |target| with matching parity.
Increase step and cumulative distance until distance-target is nonnegative and even.
An even difference can be formed by flipping a subset of steps, while an odd difference cannot; the first feasible step count is minimal.
editorial: An even difference can be formed by flipping a subset of steps, while an odd difference cannot; the first feasible step count is minimal.

tests.explanation: Moves +1 and +2 reach three in two steps.
Moves +1, +2, then -3 reach zero, so instead +1, -2, +3 reaches two in three steps.
